1  BRIEF REASONS FOR ORDER:
1. The accused has been chargesheeted for committing offences punishable under Section 336/337 of Indian Penal Code 1860, (hereinafter referred to as "IPC").
2.

It has been alleged by the prosecution that the accused Archana Gupta, who was a contractor hired to supply Midday Meal to Sarvodya Kanya Vidyalaya situated at Mohan Garden, Uttam Nagar,
supplied the cooked meal of Kadhi Chawal in the said school on 03.09.2011, wherein a dead lizard was found in one tiffin box of a student.
Further, consequent to consuming of the said meal, various children complained of nausea and stomach pain and fell ill.

3. After conclusion of investigation, the present chargesheet was filed against the accused u/s 336/337 IPC.
4.
On receipt of chargesheet, cognizance of offence was taken.

State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 2 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 Copy of the chargesheet alongwith all annexures were supplied to the accused in terms of Section 207 Cr.P.C.
5.

After giving opportunity to state as well as accused for making submissions on charge, a charge for offence u/s 336/337 IPC was framed against the accused on 27.01.2015, to which she pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
6. Prosecution examined ten witnesses to prove its case.

7. As PW1, HC Ratan Lal was examined who stated that on 03.09.2011, one plastic tiffin box and one steel container both containing Kadhi Chawal sealed with the seal of VS was produced by SI Vijender and was deposited in the maalkhana vide mud number 4616 in the register no.19.
The said entry was Ex. PW1/A (OSR).
He further deposed that on 05.09.2011, at the request of the IO, he gave the case property to SI Vijender vide RC no.114/31 for sending it to FSL and its RC was again deposited with the malkhana.
He was not cross-
examined despite opportunity.

66 Shiv Vihar owned by Reeva Sood. She deposed that Kadhi Chawal was served to the children on that day and one of the students namely Neha Pandey of class 8 th C State Vs.

sentences.text: Since, no other witness was examined by prosecution, hence, the PE was closed and statement of accused was recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. to allow him to explain the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidences against him wherein it was stated by accused she is innocent and claimed that though the meal was prepared under her supervision but she did not herself prepared the meal rather it was prepared by her team and the meal was packed by some other team.

She further asserted that she is not personally State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 10 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 liable for any of the mis-happenings and she was not negligent in her duties.
19. Since the accused chose not to lead any evidence in her defence, therefore, DE was closed and the matter was adjourned for final arguments.
20.
Final arguments were thereafter heard on behalf of state as well as the accused.

21. In the course of final argument, it was argued by the defence counsel that nothing incriminating has been found as per the report of FSL, in the sample which was collected in the presence of the principal and the police official.
Further, it was claimed that as per the testimony of PW2 who was the principal the food was first used to be tested by the committee before it was given to the students.

It was also contended by the defence that Principal herself was not aware as to who was the head of the said committee and then upon suggestion put to her, affirmed the she herself was the head or anyone appointed by her.

Further, it has also come in her evidence that on the fateful day also, the food was tested and nothing was found and therefore, if later on the lizard was found in the meal it was for the school to explain.
The counsel also contended that Principal even could not tell the name of the teacher who received the meal on the day of the incident.
Thus, brushing away any liability on her part.

It was also pointed by the defence counsel that after the incident the same NGO continued to State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 11 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 supply the mid-day meal.
Lastly, it was averred that the committee which received the food and distributed it among the students were liable for the incident and not the accused.

22. Per-contra, it was the arguments of the Ld. APP for the state that from all the materials available on record to convict the accused as PW5 Reeva Sood who was the director of the trust has clearly testified that accused was responsible for transporting the meal to the concerned school.
Furthermore, the FSL report are not conclusive proof.
23. I have carefully considered the submissions made on behalf of the parties and have perused the case file meticulously.
24. Now this court shall appreciate the evidences one by one in order to decide whether the prosecution has been successful in proving its case.

25. The ingredients of offence U/s 336/337 IPC are that the impugned act must of rash and negligence so as to endanger human life or personal safety and hurt must have been caused to some persons by such rash or negligent act.

Also, in Mohan Shayam vs. The State (NCT of Delhi) dated 25.05.2012, wherein on the similar facts, it was held by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi that "In order to prove the act of negligence and rashness, it must be shown that the act was done without proper State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 12 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 record to its consequences and without any precautions taken for ensuring the safety of others".
27.

entities.text: Mohan Shayam vs. The State (NCT of Delhi)

sentences.text:
Criminal negligence has also been discussed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the landmark judgment of S.N. Hussain vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, AIR 1972, SC 685 as under:
"Criminal negligence on the other hand, is the gross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable proper care and precaution to guard against injuries either to the public generally or to an individual particular, which, having regard to all the circumstance out of which the charge has arisen it was the imperative duty of the accused person to have adopted.

entities.text: S.N. Hussain vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, AIR 1972, SC 685
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Culpable negligence lies in the failure to exercise reasonable and proper care and the extent of reasonableness will always depend upon the circumstances of each case".
28.

In the given case, it is the allegations of the prosecution that accused Archana Gupta, who was entrusted with the responsibility for preparing the mid-day meal which was to be supplied to Sarvodya Kanya School, was negligent in her duty and on 03.09.2011 a dead lizard was found in the plastic tiffin box of one student.

As per the statement of the school principal Smt. Pushpa Bhai, the task of supplying the mid-day meal was assigned to an NGO whose name she could not recount and thereafter, Smt. Reeva Sood who was the trustee State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 13 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 of Indcare Trust by which the said mid-day meal was supplied to the school had stated that as per the SPA Mark X, which was executed in favour of Mrs. Archana Gupta was assigned the job of preparing and distributing the mid-day meal.

The Indcare Trust was assigned the work to supply the mid-day meal in Sarvodya School of Govt. of Delhi situated in Zone no.14 and no.18 by a Govt. Order and thereafter, the accused was tasked with taking care of the work of supplying the cooked meal / mid-day meal in Sarvodaya School and she was authorized for Kitchen Cooperation of Meal as per the standard prescribed by the Government.

29. From the above, it is clear that accused was in-charge of preparing and supplying of the mid-day meal to the school, however, before any liability can be fixed on the accused, it has to be seen that there was no break in the chain from the point the cooked meal was prepared and packed, till the time it reached into the plates of the students and very apparently this is not the situation in the present case.
It is perceptible from the statement of student Neha Pandey, who so received the meal with the dead lizard, that the meal was served to her in her tiffin box in the school itself.

Now, it is not clear if the dead lizard was already there in the container in which the meal was kept or it fell in her tiffin box while the meal was being served i.e., the possibility of lizard having fallen in the tiffin box while the meal was being served.

State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 14 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 State vs . Archana Gupta on 25 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171946125/
7 30.

Moreover, the case of the prosecution also becomes doubtful, keeping in view the testimony of school principal as during her cross- examination, a new fact came to the light that there was also a committee in the school to distribute the mid-day meal (amongst the students) and in this respect she also confirmed the suggestion of the counsel that she is the head of the said committee.

It was also stated by her that before food was distributed it was first tested/tasted in the school and also,
that firstly the food was tasted by her and then by the committee and the said process was also followed on the day of the incident also but on the day of the incident neither she nor any other teacher tasted/tested the food.
This shows the lack of vigilance and negligence even on the part of the school, the principal of the school could not even remember the teacher who received the midday meal on the fateful day.

31. It is also not clear if the food that was supplied, was supplied in the individual tiffin boxes to be handed out to the students or it was supplied in a bulk to be served individually to the students in their tiffin boxes either brought by them or provided by the school for that purpose, as this also paves a way for an escape clause to the accused and makes it unreasonable to attach any the criminal liability upon the accused.
32. So far, what the court can gather from the records is that there were containers in which the meal was supplied and it was served to the students in their tiffin boxes.

Hence, if the food was checked when State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 15 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 it was so received in the school as it is reflected from the statement of the PW2 i.e., the principal of the school, then how the lizard came to be found in the food?
Is a question which should be asked to and should be answerable by the school concerned.
Thus, only the accused cannot be held liable in the present circumstances if there are chances that such a lapse might have occurred due to the negligence of the school authorities also.

33. Furthermore, though the students complained of nausea and stomach pain but it happened only after the news, regarding a dead lizard in the food spread in the school, which might as well be the case of psychological effects because as per the MLC of the school students all vitals were reported to be stable and no serious health conditions were reported for any of the students.

According to the FSL report also, no poisonousness substance was detected in sample which was also comprised of the container of kadhi chawal and also a tiffin box in which the lizard was allegedly found.
There is also no photograph of the said tiffin box in which the said dead lizard was found.

34. Thus, in the attendance of so many ambiguities and flaws, the conviction of the accused cannot be justified as it is the most sacrosanct principle of criminal justice that any offence should be proved beyond reasonable doubts against the accused before he/she can be held liable i.e., the evidences should be proved in such a compact manner that it should be impervious to any let-out clause for State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 16 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 the accused.

35. Hence, in view of the aforesaid discussions and reasons, it can conclusively, be held that Prosecution has failed to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubts and therefore,
the accused Archana Gupta W/o Sh. Subhash Gupta, is acquitted of charge U/s 336/337 IPC.

It is perceptible from the statement of student Neha Pandey, who so received the meal with the dead lizard, that the meal was served to her in her tiffin box in the school itself.
Now, it is not clear if the dead lizard was already there in the container in which the meal was kept or it fell in her tiffin box while the meal was being served i.e., the possibility of lizard having fallen in the tiffin box while the meal was being served.
This shows the lack of vigilance and negligence even on the part of the school, the principal of the school could not even remember the teacher who received the midday meal on the fateful day.
31. It is also not clear if the food that was supplied, was supplied in the individual tiffin boxes to be handed out to the students or it was supplied in a bulk to be served individually to the students in their tiffin boxes either brought by them or provided by the school for that purpose, as this also paves a way for an escape clause to the accused and makes it unreasonable to attach any the criminal liability upon the accused.
32. So far, what the court can gather from the records is that there were containers in which the meal was supplied and it was served to the students in their tiffin boxes.
Is a question which should be asked to and should be answerable by the school concerned.
Thus, only the accused cannot be held liable in the present circumstances if there are chances that such a lapse might have occurred due to the negligence of the school authorities also.
33. Furthermore, though the students complained of nausea and stomach pain but it happened only after the news, regarding a dead lizard in the food spread in the school, which might as well be the case of psychological effects because as per the MLC of the school students all vitals were reported to be stable and no serious health conditions were reported for any of the students.
There is also no photograph of the said tiffin box in which the said dead lizard was found.
34. Thus, in the attendance of so many ambiguities and flaws, the conviction of the accused cannot be justified as it is the most sacrosanct principle of criminal justice that any offence should be proved beyond reasonable doubts against the accused before he/she can be held liable i.e., the evidences should be proved in such a compact manner that it should be impervious to any let-out clause for State Vs. Archana Gupta FIR No.384/2011, PS Uttam Nagar, Page No. 16 of 17 Judgment dated 25.08.2022 the accused.
opennyai_summary.decision:
35. Hence, in view of the aforesaid discussions and reasons, it can conclusively, be held that Prosecution has failed to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubts and therefore,
the accused Archana Gupta W/o Sh. Subhash Gupta, is acquitted of charge U/s 336/337 IPC.
Ordered Accordingly.
